Normal PaO2 with falsely reassuring calculated ABG saturation → saturation gap versus measured pulse oximetry
Routine blood gas oxygen saturation calculation cannot exclude dyshemoglobinemia
Check CBC, lactate, exposure history; assess G6PD status when feasible without delaying urgent management

rows.label: Tx
items: Stop exposure, give high-flow oxygen; mild asymptomatic cases → observation and serial levels
★ Symptomatic or MetHb ≥20–30% → **methylene blue 1–2 mg/kg IV**; lower threshold with limited reserve
★ **G6PD deficiency** → avoid methylene blue; ascorbic acid, specialist-guided exchange transfusion for severe disease
Methylene blue + serotonergic drugs → serotonin toxicity risk; seek toxicology advice
Refractory severe disease → exchange transfusion or hyperbaric oxygen; monitor for dapsone-associated rebound

rows.label: Complications
items: Tissue hypoxia, lactic acidosis, cardiovascular collapse, neurologic injury
Excess methylene blue can cause hemolysis and paradoxical worsening

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid recurrent oxidant exposure; document offending drug and counsel about OTC topical anesthetics
Safe infant water supply; medical alert identification for hereditary disease

rows.label: Mimics
items: Carbon monoxide: pulse oximetry often falsely normal; elevated carboxyhemoglobin
Sulfhemoglobinemia: sulfur exposure, persistent cyanosis, no response to methylene blue
Pulmonary hypoxemia: reduced PaO2 generally tracks impaired oxygenation

microcytic-anemia.name: Microcytic anemia
microcytic-anemia.scope: Iron deficiency, anemia of chronic disease, thalassemia, sideroblastic anemia
microcytic-anemia.core: Low hemoglobin with MCV <80 fL: distinguish depleted iron, inflammatory iron sequestration, globin underproduction, and defective heme synthesis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Menstrual/GI blood loss, pregnancy, low intake, malabsorption → iron depletion
Chronic infection, autoimmune disease, malignancy → inflammatory anemia
Inherited hemoglobin disorders; alcohol, lead, isoniazid, myelodysplasia → disordered heme production
Preterm birth → low stores, screen toddlers; infant microcytosis → **dietary history** for excess cow's milk

rows.label: Clues
items: Fatigue, pallor, exertional dyspnea; severe anemia → tachycardia, angina, syncope
Pica, koilonychia, restless legs suggest iron deficiency
Markedly low MCV, preserved hemoglobin, high RBC count, **normal RDW** (Mentzer <13) suggest thalassemia trait

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Inflammation → ↑hepcidin → ferroportin suppression, impaired absorption and iron release; cytokines blunt **erythropoietin**
Sideroblasts: mitochondrial iron accumulation in erythroblasts from impaired protoporphyrin synthesis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CBC/smear → ferritin**, iron, TIBC, transferrin saturation; ferritin rises with inflammation
★ Ferritin **<45 ng/mL in anemia** supports iron deficiency; normal result cannot exclude during inflammation
★ Adult men/postmenopausal women with iron deficiency → **EGD + colonoscopy**; consider celiac testing
Hemoglobin electrophoresis for suspected beta-thalassemia; alpha trait may require genetic testing; exposure → blood lead
Microcytosis + afebrile pain crisis, at-risk ancestry → **smear** for sickled cells (sickle–β-thalassemia)

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Iron deficiency → **oral ferrous sulfate**; intolerance/malabsorption or rapid replacement need → IV iron
Treat bleeding source; continue iron about 3 months beyond hemoglobin normalization; reassess nonresponse
Inflammatory anemia → treat underlying disease; selected CKD → iron ± erythropoietin
Sideroblastic: remove trigger, pyridoxine if isoniazid-related; severe thalassemia → transfusion/chelation

rows.label: Complications
items: Iron deficiency: developmental effects in children, adverse pregnancy outcomes
Repeated transfusion → iron overload, cardiac/hepatic injury; oral iron → constipation, dark stool
Four-gene α-deletion → **Hb Barts** (γ4) → severe fetal anemia, hydrops fetalis

rows.label: Prevention
items: Adequate dietary iron, pregnancy supplementation, lead-exposure reduction
★ **No empiric long-term iron for thalassemia trait** without documented deficiency

rows.label: Mimics
items: Acute blood loss: initially normocytic; hemoglobin may lag volume loss
Hemolysis: reticulocytosis, ↑LDH/indirect bilirubin, ↓haptoglobin

microcytic-anemia.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [AGA iron deficiency evaluation 2020](https://gastro.org/clinical-guidance/gastrointestinal-evaluation-of-iron-deficiency-anemia/); remaining hematology established teaching.

newborn-screening.name: Newborn screening
newborn-screening.scope: Congenital hypothyroidism (macroglossia, umbilical hernia, levothyroxine), phenylketonuria, galactosemia, congenital adrenal hyperplasia, hemoglobinopathies, cystic fibrosis, pulse oximetry, hearing screen
newborn-screening.core: Screen apparently healthy newborns for treatable metabolic, endocrine, genetic, cardiac, and hearing disorders before symptoms or irreversible injury.

rows.label: Who
items: All newborns; blood-spot panels vary by state; also screen cardiac oxygenation and hearing

rows.label: Start/stop
items: ★ Heel stick **24–48 hours**; early collection, transfusion, prematurity may require repeats
Pulse oximetry ≥24 hours or before early discharge; hearing by 1 month

rows.label: Test
items: ★ Cardiac pass: **≥95% in both right hand and foot**, difference ≤3 percentage points
<90% anywhere → immediate failure; otherwise **one repeat** in 1 hour (older algorithms: two)
Hearing: otoacoustic emissions or auditory brainstem response; NICU → brainstem-based screen

rows.label: IF positive
items: ★ Critical result → confirm promptly without delaying lifesaving treatment
Failed cardiac screen → evaluate hypoxemia, echocardiography; ductal-dependent lesion → prostaglandin E1
★ Failed hearing → diagnostic audiology by **3 months**, intervention by **6 months**

rows.label: Traps
items: Normal examination does not exclude disease; hypothyroidism later causes macroglossia/umbilical hernia
Ill infant with suspected CAH → treat despite pending screen; no diagnostic reassurance
Hereditary fructose intolerance: symptoms only after fructose/sucrose, so not on breast milk alone

table.title: Urgent positive blood-spot results
rows: Start levothyroxine promptly, ideally by 2 weeks
Classic galactosemia: feeding → vomiting, jaundice, hepatomegaly
Penicillin from infancy, vaccines, hematology follow-up
Specialty care, nutrition, pancreatic enzymes if insufficient

newborn-screening.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [CDC cardiac screening](https://www.cdc.gov/heart-defects/hcp/screening/), [CDC hearing](https://www.cdc.gov/hearing-loss-children/screening/); blood-spot actions established teaching.

normal-pediatric-variants.name: Normal pediatric variants
normal-pediatric-variants.scope: Thymic sail sign on chest radiograph, physiologic genu varum and valgum, tibial torsion, infantile hemangioma
normal-pediatric-variants.core: Age-appropriate anatomy and growth can resemble disease; symmetry, normal function, and expected evolution support reassurance instead of unnecessary intervention.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Normal skeletal alignment changes with development; familial rotational profiles are common
Infantile hemangiomas more frequent with prematurity, low birth weight and female sex

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Symmetric painless findings with normal growth/function** favor physiologic variation
Asymmetry, pain, progression, short stature or abnormal neurologic examination → pathologic evaluation
Hemangiomas appear in first weeks, proliferate rapidly during infancy, then gradually involute
Periocular, airway/beard-distribution, ulcerating or large segmental lesions are high-risk, not simple cosmetic variants

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Growth remodels lower-limb alignment/rotation; normal thymic tissue may silhouette against the lung
Hemangioma is a benign vascular tumor with proliferative and involution phases, distinct from vascular malformation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Typical symmetric limb variant → **clinical examination**, growth review and rotational profile
Imaging for red flags, atypical age or suspected metabolic bone disease; not routine physiologic bowing
Typical hemangioma → clinical diagnosis; ≥5 cutaneous lesions → hepatic ultrasound
Large segmental facial/lumbosacral lesion → evaluate associated structural anomalies with specialist guidance

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Reassurance and observation** for physiologic alignment, thymic appearance, toddler genital self-touching without abuse signs
Special shoes/braces do not correct internal tibial torsion; persistent severe functional deformity → orthopedics
★ High-risk hemangioma → **early referral, oral propranolol**; selected superficial lesions → topical timolol
Give propranolol with feeds, hold during poor intake/vomiting; monitor bradycardia and hypoglycemia

rows.label: Complications
items: Unnecessary imaging, bracing or surgery; hemangioma → ulceration, amblyopia, airway obstruction or residual skin change
Multiple hepatic hemangiomas → high-output heart failure or consumptive hypothyroidism

rows.label: Mimics
items: Blount disease: progressive asymmetric tibial bowing; rickets: widened wrists, abnormal mineralization
Mediastinal mass: mass effect/distortion rather than soft thymic contour

normal-pediatric-variants.evidence: Hemangioma guidance checked 2026-10-30: [AAP 2019 guideline](https://publications.aap.org/pediatrics/article/143/1/e20183475/37268/Clinical-Practice-Guideline-for-the-Management-of); skeletal variants: established teaching.

table.title: Expected developmental patterns
rows: Varum to toddler; valgum peaks age 3–4
Yellow papules on erythematous base; trunk, well neonate
Resolves in days; reassure, no cultures
Bilateral nocturnal calf pain; normal exam, massage relieves
Blue hands, feet, perioral; pink mucosa, normal SpO2
Benign, first 24–48 hours; warmer if cold

obesity-and-bariatric-surgery.name: Obesity and bariatric surgery
obesity-and-bariatric-surgery.scope: Lifestyle modifications, pharmacotherapy (GLP-1 receptor agonists), indications for bariatric surgery, postoperative nutritional and surgical complications
obesity-and-bariatric-surgery.core: Chronic excess adiposity with metabolic complications; sustained treatment combines nutrition, activity, behavioral support, medications, and sometimes metabolic surgery.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Calorie-dense diet, inactivity, sleep deprivation, genetic susceptibility, food insecurity
Glucocorticoids, antipsychotics, insulin; investigate endocrine causes when examination suggests them

rows.label: Clues
items: BMI ≥30 kg/m²; central adiposity predicts cardiometabolic risk
Screen for hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidemia, sleep apnea, fatty liver, osteoarthritis, depression

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Adipose inflammation and insulin resistance; appetite regulation favors weight regain after weight loss
Bypass and sleeve alter gut signaling and intake; bypass additionally decreases nutrient absorption

rows.label: Dx
items: Weight trajectory, medication review, eating-disorder assessment; A1c, lipids, liver enzymes
★ Postoperative **tachycardia**, fever, abdominal pain → investigate anastomotic leak urgently

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Structured calorie deficit, activity, behavioral follow-up; **5–10% weight loss** improves metabolic disease
Child: **cut liquid calories** first (juice, excess whole milk); cause is total calorie surplus
Medications: BMI ≥30, or ≥27 with comorbidity; semaglutide or tirzepatide plus lifestyle changes
★ Avoid GLP-1 agents with **MEN 2/medullary thyroid carcinoma** history; avoid weight-loss drugs during pregnancy
★ **Surgical referral** by eligibility below; assess nutritional, operative, psychosocial readiness and lifelong follow-up

rows.label: Complications
items: Early: leak, bleeding, VTE; later: stricture, rapid-weight-loss gallstones, internal hernia with intermittent pain
Roux-en-Y: dumping after sugary meals, marginal ulcers; iron, B12, calcium, vitamin D deficiencies
Persistent vomiting → thiamine deficiency; give thiamine promptly before carbohydrate loading

rows.label: Prevention
items: Lifelong supplements and nutritional surveillance after surgery; avoid NSAIDs and tobacco after bypass
Small meals, fewer simple sugars for dumping; delay conception during rapid postoperative weight loss

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cushing syndrome: violaceous striae, proximal weakness, easy bruising
Hypothyroidism: cold intolerance, bradycardia; usually modest weight gain

osteomyelitis.name: Osteomyelitis
osteomyelitis.scope: Vertebral osteomyelitis and discitis, hematogenous seeding (S. aureus, IV drug use), contiguous spread (diabetic foot ulcer), probe-to-bone test, MRI, bone biopsy and culture, parenteral antibiotics
osteomyelitis.core: Persistent focal bone or back pain, especially with bacteremia, a deep diabetic ulcer, or elevated inflammatory markers, suggests bone infection.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Hematogenous seeding: S. aureus, endocarditis, injection drug use; vertebral disease often lacks fever
Contiguous spread: diabetic foot ulcers, pressure injury; direct inoculation: open fracture, surgery, hardware
Sickle cell: Salmonella association, but S. aureus remains important; plantar puncture through shoe → Pseudomonas

rows.label: Clues
items: Point tenderness, swelling, drainage or nonhealing sinus; systemic toxicity may be absent
★ New neurologic deficit, saddle anesthesia, urinary retention → **epidural extension/cord compression**
Diabetic ulcer over bony prominence, visible bone, or prolonged failure to heal increases suspicion
Child: fever, point tenderness over long-bone **metaphysis**; septic joint instead limits joint motion

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Infected bone develops inflammatory pressure, vascular compromise, and necrosis
Sequestrum: devitalized infected bone; involucrum: reactive new bone; biofilm promotes hardware persistence

rows.label: Dx
items: CBC, ESR/CRP, two blood-culture sets; plain films first but early findings can be absent
★ Diabetic foot: **probe-to-bone** plus radiographs/inflammatory markers; MRI if diagnosis remains uncertain
★ **MRI** best for early marrow disease and epidural/paraspinal abscess; bone scan uptake if MRI unavailable
Bone biopsy for histology/culture before antibiotics if stable; superficial wound swabs unreliable
Compatible vertebral MRI plus S. aureus bacteremia usually obviates biopsy; assess endocarditis source

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Sepsis or neurologic compromise → cultures then **IV vancomycin + cefepime**, urgent surgical assessment
Stable vertebral disease → obtain microbiologic diagnosis before empiric antibiotics
MSSA → cefazolin/nafcillin; MRSA → vancomycin; tailor to cultures, usually about **6 weeks**
IV initially for serious disease; selected stable patients can complete highly bioavailable oral regimens
Debride necrotic bone/drain abscess; surgery for instability, progressive deficit, or uncontrolled infection

rows.label: Complications
items: Epidural abscess, pathologic fracture, deformity, bacteremia, chronic draining sinus
Longstanding sinus may develop squamous carcinoma; prolonged antibiotics → line infection, renal injury, C. difficile

rows.label: Prevention
items: Diabetic foot inspection, offloading, vascular assessment, glucose control; prompt open-fracture antibiotics and debridement

rows.label: Mimics
items: Charcot arthropathy: neuropathic warm foot, joint fragmentation; MRI/biopsy may distinguish overlapping infection
Bone malignancy: destructive mass, pathology without infection
Degenerative disc disease: mechanical pain without infectious endplate/disc pattern

parasitic-infections.name: Parasitic infections
parasitic-infections.scope: Strongyloidiasis, giardiasis, amebiasis, cryptosporidiosis, ascariasis, schistosomiasis, pinworm (enterobiasis), cysticercosis, eosinophilia workup, antiparasitic therapy
parasitic-infections.core: Exposure, organ pattern, and immune status identify the parasite; eosinophilia favors tissue-invasive helminths rather than intestinal protozoa.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Contaminated food/water, endemic travel, freshwater contact, barefoot soil exposure, household crowding
Steroids/HTLV-1 predispose to Strongyloides hyperinfection; advanced HIV predisposes to persistent cryptosporidiosis

rows.label: Clues
items: Ascariasis: transient cough/eosinophilic infiltrates during larval migration; later intestinal or biliary obstruction
Pinworm: nocturnal perianal/vulvar itch, dysuria with normal UA; household clustering
Cysticercosis: seizures or hydrocephalus; ingestion of **T. solium eggs**, not pork cysts
Cutaneous larva migrans: soil contact; pruritic **serpiginous tracks**; animal hookworm larvae → albendazole or ivermectin

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Giardia blunts microvilli → **fat/carbohydrate malabsorption**; invasive protozoa can affect liver, urinary tract, or CNS
Strongyloides autoinfection permits lifelong persistence and dissemination after immunosuppression

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Unexplained **eosinophilia** → travel/drug history, serial stool O&P, targeted Strongyloides serology
★ Steroids + eosinophilia or infiltrates → **Strongyloides hyperinfection**: **duodenal aspirate** larvae; stool O&P often misses
Diarrhea → stool antigen/PCR for protozoa; single routine O&P can miss infection
★ Pinworm → **morning tape test** before washing; stool testing insensitive
Brain MRI/CT for cysticercosis; eye examination before antiparasitics; assess lesion viability and location

rows.label: Tx
items: Rehydrate; ascariasis → albendazole; bowel obstruction → surgical evaluation before deworming
Pinworm → albendazole, mebendazole, or pyrantel; repeat after **2 weeks**, treat household simultaneously
★ Viable parenchymal cysticercosis → albendazole ± praziquantel with corticosteroids; seizures → levetiracetam
Calcified brain lesions → no antiparasitic; hydrocephalus → neurosurgical control before cysticidal treatment

rows.label: Complications
items: Strongyloides hyperinfection → gram-negative sepsis, respiratory failure; eosinophilia may disappear
Amebic liver abscess; schistosomiasis → portal hypertension or bladder squamous carcinoma

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Screen/treat Strongyloides before **immunosuppression** after endemic exposure
Safe water, sanitation, handwashing, footwear; avoid endemic freshwater and untreated swimming water
Neurocysticercosis household contacts → **stool O&P** to find egg-shedding T. solium tapeworm carrier

rows.label: Mimics
items: IBD: chronic inflammatory diarrhea after infection excluded
Drug hypersensitivity: eosinophilia linked to new medication, rash or organ injury

table.title: Exposure → diagnosis and treatment
rows: Camping; greasy stool, bloating; stool antigen
Dysentery, flask-shaped ulcers; stool PCR; abscess → serology
Soil; larva currens, larvae in stool
Ivermectin; hyperinfection requires prolonged daily treatment
Freshwater; hematuria (haematobium), portal fibrosis (mansoni/japonicum); eggs, serology
Confirmed E. histolytica without invasive disease

pneumonia.name: Pneumonia
pneumonia.scope: Community-acquired, hospital-acquired, ventilator-associated, aspiration, atypical pneumonia (Legionella, Mycoplasma)
pneumonia.core: Acute lower respiratory infection with a new infiltrate; severity, acquisition setting, and resistance risks determine disposition and empiric antibiotics.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, COPD, age, immunosuppression
Dysphagia, absent gag/cough (stroke, dementia, Parkinson), impaired consciousness → aspiration
HAP ≥48 hours hospitalized; VAP ≥48 hours after intubation
Prior MRSA/Pseudomonas isolation or recent hospitalization with IV antibiotics → resistant pathogens

rows.label: Clues
items: Fever, cough, sputum, focal crackles; older adults: confusion; children: lower-lobe disease may refer abdominal pain
★ Severe: **hypoxemia, hypotension, tachypnea**, multilobar disease; ventilation or pressors → ICU
Legionella: water exposure, diarrhea, hyponatremia; Mycoplasma: school-age/young adult, indolent dry cough, cold agglutinins
Immunocompromised, diffuse bilateral interstitial/alveolar infiltrates, exertional hypoxemia → **Pneumocystis**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Alveolar inflammation/exudate → shunt and impaired oxygenation
Chemical aspiration pneumonitis: sterile gastric injury; severity tracks **volume and acidity**; rapid improvement possible

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CXR** first; CT if strong suspicion despite nondiagnostic radiograph
**CURB-65** 0–1 or low PSI → outpatient; severe CAP → blood/sputum cultures, Legionella antigen ± PCR
Low procalcitonin alone does not justify withholding initial antibiotics in radiographically confirmed bacterial CAP
Gram-positive lancet diplococci → **S pneumoniae**: commonest CAP; lobar consolidation, high fever, often post-viral URI
Small gram-negative coccobacilli, smoker/COPD → **H influenzae**

rows.label: Tx
items: Oxygen, fluids for hypoperfusion; drain empyema; narrow antibiotics to cultures
★ Aspiration pneumonia: usual CAP coverage; **add anaerobic coverage only for abscess/empyema**
Anaerobes: **ampicillin-sulbactam**; older exam questions may expect **clindamycin**, even without abscess
Stable nonsevere CAP: ATS 2025 permits 3–4 days; classic ≥5-day rule remains for severe disease
★ Severe noninfluenza CAP → consider **systemic corticosteroids**; nonsevere CAP → avoid routine steroids

rows.label: Complications
items: Parapneumonic effusion, empyema, bacteremia, respiratory failure, sepsis
S aureus: postinfluenza necrotizing pneumonia; child failing amoxicillin, dense consolidation/effusion
Aspiration (alcoholism, intubation) → **lung abscess**: dependent-segment cavity, air-fluid level, foul sputum
Antibiotic exposure → C difficile

rows.label: Prevention
items: Influenza/pneumococcal vaccination, smoking cessation, swallowing evaluation
Aspiration/VAP prevention: head elevation 30–45°, oral care, early liberation from ventilation

rows.label: Mimics
items: PE: thrombotic risk, pleuritic pain, no infectious source
HF: bilateral edema, elevated JVP, cardiac dysfunction

table.title: Empiric adult regimens
rows: Amoxicillin/clavulanate + azithromycin; doxycycline alternative; or levofloxacin
Antipseudomonal: cefepime, ceftazidime, or piperacillin/tazobactam; usually 7 days

pneumothorax.name: Pneumothorax
pneumothorax.scope: Spontaneous pneumothorax (primary, secondary), tension pneumothorax, needle decompression, chest tube thoracostomy
pneumothorax.core: Pleural air causes acute unilateral pleuritic pain and reduced breath sounds; circulatory compromise indicates tension physiology requiring immediate decompression.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Primary: tall thin young adults, smoking, family history
Secondary: COPD, cystic fibrosis, PJP, interstitial lung disease; trauma/procedures or positive-pressure ventilation

rows.label: Clues
items: Unilateral hyperresonance, dyspnea, asymmetric chest expansion; severity depends on underlying reserve
★ **Hypotension + distended neck veins + unilateral absent breath sounds** → tension; tracheal deviation is late
Ventilated: positive pressure converts occult pneumothorax to tension; sudden desaturation, rising airway pressure, collapse

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Loss of negative pleural pressure permits lung collapse
One-way air entry increases intrathoracic pressure, reducing venous return and causing obstructive shock

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Unstable tension suspicion → **clinical diagnosis; no imaging delay**
Stable → upright chest radiograph: visceral pleural line with absent peripheral markings
Bedside ultrasound: absent sliding/B-lines supports; lung point highly specific; absent sliding alone nonspecific
CT for uncertain/complex cases; supine radiograph may show deep sulcus rather than apical air

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Tension → **immediate needle or finger thoracostomy**, then chest tube; oxygen and resuscitation
Needle commonly fourth/fifth intercostal space anterior/midaxillary, or second midclavicular; insert above rib
★ Minimal symptoms, stable: primary (any size) or small iatrogenic → **observation**, reliable follow-up
Symptomatic/large primary → aspiration or small-bore chest tube; secondary generally admit, drain if symptomatic/significant
Persistent air leak, recurrence, bilateral disease, or high-risk occupation → VATS bleb treatment/pleurodesis

rows.label: Complications
items: Respiratory failure, tension progression, recurrence; reexpansion pulmonary edema after drainage
Chest tube → bleeding, infection, organ injury; blocked/clamped drain may recreate tension

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Smoking cessation**; avoid flying until radiographic resolution and clearance
Scuba diving contraindicated without specialist assessment/definitive prevention; counsel recurrence warning symptoms

rows.label: Mimics
items: PE: pleuritic pain with preserved lung sliding, embolic risk
Giant bulla: intraparenchymal thin wall; CT if stable uncertainty before tube
Tamponade: shock with pericardial fluid rather than unilateral absent ventilation
Massive hemothorax: dullness, collapsed neck veins rather than distended

pneumothorax.evidence: Conservative care checked 2026-10-30: [BTS pleural guideline 2023](https://doi.org/10.1136/thorax-2022-219784); tension rescue: established emergency teaching.

potassium-disorders.name: Potassium disorders
potassium-disorders.scope: Hyperkalemia, hypokalemia, cardiac membrane stabilization, shift therapy, elimination
potassium-disorders.core: Potassium abnormalities can cause weakness and fatal arrhythmias; stabilize cardiac risk while identifying the cause and correcting total-body balance.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Hyperkalemia: AKI/CKD, RAAS blockers, potassium-sparing diuretics, tissue lysis, insulin deficiency
Hypokalemia: GI losses, loop/thiazide diuretics, hyperaldosteronism, insulin/beta-agonists, magnesium depletion

rows.label: Clues
items: Flaccid weakness, paralysis, palpitations; symptoms may be absent despite dangerous levels
★ **K ≥6.5 mmol/L, ECG changes, or rapid rise** → emergency; normal ECG not reassuring
Bradycardia/high-degree AV block with renal failure → suspect hyperkalemia; calcium before pacemaker

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Extracellular K changes alter membrane excitability and cardiac conduction
Acidosis/insulin deficiency shift K outward; intracellular shifts can coexist with severe total-body depletion

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **ECG + repeat potassium**, creatinine, glucose, bicarbonate, magnesium; assess drugs and acid-base status
Hemolysis, thrombocytosis/leukocytosis → pseudohyperkalemia; repeat atraumatic draw if clinically compatible
Hypokalemia: urine K distinguishes renal wasting from extrarenal loss; interpret with BP/acid-base pattern
Do not delay treatment for confirmatory blood draw when malignant ECG changes present

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Hyperkalemic ECG changes or dialysis-patient arrest → **IV calcium gluconate/chloride first**; protects myocardium only
★ Shift K inward: **IV insulin + dextrose**, nebulized albuterol; bicarbonate mainly with significant acidosis
Remove K: loop diuretic if urine output, selected binders; urgent dialysis for severe refractory/renal-failure cases
Mild/stable hypokalemia → oral KCl; <2.5, arrhythmia, paralysis, or no oral access → monitored IV replacement
★ **Correct magnesium deficiency** for refractory low K; never give IV potassium push; monitor glucose after insulin

rows.label: Complications
items: Ventricular arrhythmia, cardiac arrest, respiratory muscle failure
Overcorrection, rebound dyskalemia; insulin-induced hypoglycemia; IV potassium extravasation/phlebitis
Diuretic hypokalemia → **digoxin toxicity**, multifocal PVCs; check K first

rows.label: Prevention
items: Review supplements/salt substitutes; monitor K/creatinine after diuretic or RAAS-drug changes
Treat diarrhea/vomiting and underlying mineralocorticoid disorders; replace ongoing losses

rows.label: Mimics
items: Guillain-Barré: ascending areflexic weakness without explanatory electrolyte pattern
Periodic paralysis: episodic shifts, sometimes thyrotoxicosis; avoid excessive replacement causing rebound

table.title: ECG patterns
rows: Peaked T → PR prolongation → wide QRS/sine-wave
Flat T, ST depression, prominent U waves

potassium-disorders.evidence: Not checked online; established electrolyte emergency principles.

primary-immunodeficiencies.name: Primary immunodeficiencies
primary-immunodeficiencies.scope: Selective IgA deficiency, common variable immunodeficiency (CVID), X-linked agammaglobulinemia, severe combined immunodeficiency, hyper-IgE syndrome, Wiskott-Aldrich, chronic granulomatous disease
primary-immunodeficiencies.core: Recurrent, unusually severe, persistent, or opportunistic infections; organism pattern and age of onset localize the immune defect.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Consanguinity, affected relatives, male relatives dying in infancy; absent family history does not exclude disease

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Failure to thrive, chronic diarrhea, persistent thrush, or infections across multiple organ systems
Deep abscesses suggest phagocyte dysfunction; recurrent encapsulated bacteria suggest impaired antibody function

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Selective IgA deficiency: impaired mucosal defense; respiratory infections, giardiasis, atopy, or no symptoms
Antibody disorders impair opsonization; T-cell defects permit viral, fungal, and protozoal opportunists
DiGeorge: 3rd/4th **pharyngeal pouch** failure → absent thymus, hypocalcemia, conotruncal defects, T-cell infections
ADA deficiency: autosomal recessive SCID; toxic deoxyadenosine destroys T and B cells

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Start **CBC with differential, quantitative immunoglobulins**, HIV testing; assess vaccine antibody responses
Lymphocyte subsets distinguish B-cell and T-cell deficiencies; abnormal results → genetic confirmation
IgA deficiency: isolated IgA <7 mg/dL after age 4 years; normal IgG and IgM
★ Newborn **TREC screen** detects impaired T-cell production before symptomatic SCID

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Profound combined immune failure → isolation, irradiated CMV-negative blood products, urgent **transplant evaluation**
Acute infections: organism-directed antimicrobials; immunoglobulin replacement not useful for isolated IgA deficiency

rows.label: Complications
items: Bronchiectasis, chronic enteropathy, autoimmune disease; CVID additionally increases lymphoma risk
Anti-IgA antibodies can cause anaphylaxis to blood products

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Avoid **live vaccines** in major T-cell defects; immunize household contacts with safe vaccine choices
IgA-related transfusion reactions → washed cellular products or IgA-deficient plasma
CGD: TMP-SMX + itraconazole prophylaxis; genetic counseling for inherited defects

rows.label: Mimics
items: Vertical HIV: bacterial infections + zoster, nodes, maternal opportunistic infection; low CD4, positive virologic testing
Secondary hypogammaglobulinemia: nephrotic protein loss, B-cell malignancy, or rituximab exposure

table.title: Defect fingerprints
rows: Adolescent/adult; low IgG, poor vaccine response
Boy after 6 months; absent tonsils/B cells
Infant; absent thymic shadow, profound lymphopenia
Cold abscesses, eczema, retained teeth, pneumatoceles

primary-immunodeficiencies.evidence: Not checked online; established clinical immunology teaching.

pubertal-development.name: Pubertal development
pubertal-development.scope: Tanner stages, normal thelarche vs breast mass, premature adrenarche, precocious puberty, constitutional delay of growth and puberty
pubertal-development.core: Interpret sexual maturation by sequence, age, growth velocity, and bone age; isolated benign variants lack progressive gonadal activation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Constitutional delay often familial; chronic illness, undernutrition, excess exercise delay maturation
CNS lesions, gonadal/adrenal hormone excess, exogenous sex steroids can cause early puberty

rows.label: Clues
items: Girls: breast budding precedes peak growth, then menarche about 2–3 years later
Boys: testes enlarge before penile growth; pubic hair reflects adrenarche, not necessarily gonadarche
★ Asymmetric tender **subareolar breast bud** at expected age usually normal; hard eccentric mass needs evaluation
Rapid height acceleration, advancing secondary characteristics, neurologic symptoms → pathologic early maturation concern

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Central puberty: hypothalamic GnRH pulsatility → LH/FSH → gonadal steroids
Adrenarche produces adrenal androgens independently; peripheral hormone excess suppresses pituitary gonadotropins
Immature hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis → irregular anovulatory cycles, normal for 2–3 years after menarche
Virilized boy with **prepubertal testes** → peripheral androgen, usually adrenal; central puberty enlarges testes

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Precocious: secondary sexual development **before 8 years girls or 9 years boys**
★ Delayed: **no breasts by 13**, no testes ≥4 mL by 14; evaluate absent menarche by 15
Growth chart, Tanner examination, bone age; LH/FSH, estradiol/testosterone, TSH selected by pattern
Central precocity → pubertal basal/stimulated LH; brain MRI especially boys, young girls, neurologic signs
Peripheral pattern → targeted adrenal/gonadal tests/imaging; isolated adrenarche requires exclusion of rapid virilization

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Progressive central precocity → **GnRH agonist**; treat CNS cause when present
Peripheral precocity → remove hormone source or treat tumor/adrenal disorder; GnRH agonist alone ineffective
Constitutional delay → reassurance, follow growth; distress → specialist-guided brief sex-steroid course
Benign premature thelarche/adrenarche → observe progression; no automatic hormonal treatment
Pubertal gynecomastia, unilateral or bilateral, smooth subareolar → **reassurance**; no labs/biopsy; carcinoma very rare

rows.label: Complications
items: Early epiphyseal closure → reduced adult height; psychosocial distress
Missed hypogonadism → impaired bone accrual; untreated CNS/tumor cause may progress

rows.label: Prevention
items: Adequate nutrition, manage chronic disease, avoid household hormone exposure; serial growth surveillance
Normal puberty + moodiness, mild parent conflict → **puberty education** for child, parents; no drug testing

rows.label: Mimics
items: Primary gonadal failure: high LH/FSH, low sex steroids
Permanent central hypogonadism: absent progression rather than eventual familial catch-up
Familial short stature: short parents, bone age matches chronologic age; constitutional delay: **delayed bone age**

table.title: Tanner staging anchors
rows: Further enlargement; menarche usually within 1–2 years

pubertal-development.evidence: Not checked online; established pediatric endocrine timing and Tanner staging.

pulmonary-hypertension.name: Pulmonary hypertension
pulmonary-hypertension.scope: WHO groups 1-5 (PAH, left heart disease, lung disease/hypoxia, CTEPH, multifactorial), cor pulmonale, echocardiography, right heart catheterization, endothelin receptor antagonists, PDE-5 inhibitors
pulmonary-hypertension.core: Progressive exertional dyspnea, syncope or right-heart failure with elevated pulmonary pressures requires hemodynamic classification before vasodilator treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Connective-tissue disease, congenital shunts, portal hypertension, HIV, methamphetamine → PAH
Left-heart disease, chronic lung disease/hypoxia or prior pulmonary embolism are common secondary contexts

rows.label: Clues
items: Loud P2, RV heave, tricuspid regurgitation murmur; exertional chest pain or presyncope
JVD, hepatomegaly and edema → right-heart failure/cor pulmonale
Severe dyspnea with relatively preserved spirometry or low DLCO suggests pulmonary vascular disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Pulmonary vascular resistance or elevated left filling pressure increases RV afterload
Sustained pressure overload → RV hypertrophy, dilation, reduced output and systemic venous congestion
Chronic alveolar hypoxia (COPD, OSA) → **pulmonary vasoconstriction** and remodeling → raised vascular resistance

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Echocardiography** estimates probability and evaluates RV/left-heart function; not definitive pressure diagnosis
★ **Right-heart catheterization: mean PAP >20 mm Hg** at rest confirms PH
Precapillary: wedge ≤15 mm Hg and **PVR >2 Wood units**; postcapillary: wedge >15
★ **V/Q scan** screens CTEPH; normal perfusion essentially excludes chronic thromboembolic disease
PFT/DLCO, chest CT, sleep evaluation, HIV/autoimmune testing by history; vasoreactivity testing in selected PAH

rows.label: Tx
items: Oxygen for hypoxemia, diuresis for congestion; treat underlying disease and refer confirmed PAH/CTEPH
★ PAH → specialist **endothelin antagonist + PDE-5 inhibitor**; high-risk disease → parenteral prostacyclin
Vasoreactive idiopathic/heritable/drug-associated PAH → selected high-dose calcium-channel blocker; not empiric treatment
CTEPH → lifelong anticoagulation and pulmonary endarterectomy if operable; selected balloon angioplasty or riociguat
Do not routinely use PAH vasodilators for left-heart/lung-disease PH; PDE-5 drugs cannot combine with nitrates/riociguat

rows.label: Complications
items: RV failure, arrhythmia, syncope and death; pregnancy carries substantial maternal risk in PAH
Endothelin antagonists are teratogenic; some require liver monitoring

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid methamphetamine, address thromboembolic risk; vaccination, supervised exercise, pregnancy/contraception counseling

rows.label: Mimics
items: HFpEF: elevated wedge pressure identifies postcapillary cause
Deconditioning/anemia: no catheter-confirmed pulmonary pressure elevation

rh-alloimmunization.name: Rh alloimmunization
rh-alloimmunization.scope: Rh(D) and other red cell alloimmunization (Kell, Duffy), anti-D immune globulin prophylaxis, indirect Coombs titer monitoring, fetomaternal hemorrhage (Kleihauer-Betke), middle cerebral artery Doppler for fetal anemia
rh-alloimmunization.core: Maternal IgG against fetal red-cell antigens crosses the placenta, causing fetal anemia, hydrops, and neonatal hemolysis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Antigen-negative mother/positive fetus; prior pregnancy, transfusion, bleeding, trauma, invasive procedures
Anti-D, anti-Kell, and anti-Duffy clinically significant; ABO incompatibility usually milder

rows.label: Clues
items: Often asymptomatic mother; fetal ascites, skin edema, placentomegaly, cardiomegaly
Neonate: early jaundice, pallor, reticulocytosis, **positive direct Coombs**; severe disease → cardiovascular collapse

rows.label: Pathophys
items: First exposure sensitizes; subsequent antigen exposure produces an anamnestic response
Kell antibodies additionally suppress erythropoiesis; low titers can still cause severe disease

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ First prenatal visit: ABO/Rh type + **indirect Coombs**; repeat before routine antenatal prophylaxis
Antibody → **paternal antigen typing**; negative (certain paternity) → no fetal risk; else fetal typing, titers
★ Critical titer, often **1:16**, or previously affected pregnancy → middle cerebral artery Doppler
MCA peak systolic velocity >1.5 MoM → fetal blood sampling; Kell warrants specialist surveillance
Kleihauer-Betke quantifies hemorrhage for dosing: **300 µg covers 30 mL fetal whole blood**

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Severe preterm fetal anemia → **intrauterine transfusion**; near term → delivery
Neonatal hyperbilirubinemia → phototherapy; severe hemolysis → exchange transfusion

rows.label: Complications
items: High-output heart failure, stillbirth, bilirubin encephalopathy, delayed neonatal anemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Unsensitized Rh-negative mother: **anti-D immune globulin** at 28 weeks and within 72 hours postpartum
Sensitizing event → dose now; lasts ~12 weeks, repeat at 28; postpartum only if Rh-positive/unknown infant
★ Established anti-D sensitization → prophylaxis ineffective; no equivalent prophylaxis for Kell/Duffy
ACOG 2024: routine Rh testing/prophylaxis may be forgone for abortion/loss before 12 weeks

rows.label: Mimics
items: Parvovirus: nonimmune hydrops with negative maternal antibody screen
ABO hemolysis: may affect first pregnancy; fetal hydrops uncommon

rh-alloimmunization.evidence: Prophylaxis checked 2026-10-30: [ACOG Rh guidance](https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/the-rh-factor-how-it-can-affect-your-pregnancy), [2024 update](https://doi.org/10.1097/AOG.0000000000005733); remaining content established teaching.

secondary-hypertension.name: Secondary hypertension
secondary-hypertension.scope: Renal artery stenosis, primary hyperaldosteronism, pheochromocytoma, Cushing syndrome, coarctation of aorta, diagnostic workup
secondary-hypertension.core: Abrupt, unusually young, severe, or resistant hypertension suggests a treatable secondary driver.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Renal stenosis: older smoker → atherosclerotic **lipid plaque**; young/middle-aged woman → **fibromuscular dysplasia** (medial hyperplasia, renal + carotid)
Renal disease, adrenal tumors, sleep apnea
NSAIDs, oral contraceptives, stimulants, glucocorticoids, licorice; medication nonadherence can mimic resistance

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Hypokalemia + metabolic alkalosis** → aldosterone excess, primary or renovascular; normal K does not exclude it
**Abdominal bruit**, diffuse atherosclerosis, late abrupt worsening, small unilateral kidney → renal artery stenosis
Flash pulmonary edema or creatinine rise >30% after ACE inhibitor/ARB → renovascular disease
**Episodic headache, sweating, palpitations** → pheochromocytoma; cushingoid appearance, upper-body hypertension guide testing

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Renal hypoperfusion → juxtaglomerular **renin** → RAAS; ACE inhibitor removes efferent constriction → ↓renal flow, ↓GFR across stenosis
Autonomous aldosterone → distal sodium absorption, potassium loss, low renin; pressure natriuresis escape prevents edema
Adrenal medullary catecholamine or cortisol excess, aortic obstruction, or nocturnal hypoxia increases vascular pressure

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Confirm **home/ambulatory BP**, adherence, cuff technique; BMP, urinalysis, creatinine, TSH
Sleep-apnea symptoms → polysomnography; abnormal urinary sediment → renal ultrasound and kidney evaluation
★ Biochemical testing precedes adrenal imaging; correct hypokalemia and account for interfering medications
Endocrine Society 2025: suggest **aldosterone screening for all hypertension**, conditional on resources

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Primary aldosteronism: unilateral → **adrenalectomy**; bilateral → spironolactone/eplerenone
Renovascular atherosclerosis → medical risk reduction; revascularize selected recurrent pulmonary edema or refractory disease
Fibromuscular dysplasia → angioplasty; critical bilateral renal stenosis → avoid ACE inhibitor/ARB
★ Pheochromocytoma: **alpha blockade before beta blockade**, volume expansion, then surgery
Treat cortisol source, repair significant coarctation, use CPAP for OSA; stop contributing drugs

rows.label: Complications
items: Stroke, MI, heart failure, CKD, retinopathy
Unopposed alpha stimulation after beta blockade can cause catecholamine crisis

rows.label: Prevention
items: Monitor renal function/K after RAAS blockers or mineralocorticoid antagonists
Genetic evaluation/family screening for suspected hereditary pheochromocytoma or congenital aortic disease

rows.label: Mimics
items: White-coat hypertension: normal out-of-office readings
Essential hypertension: gradual course without specific endocrine/renal clues

table.title: Targeted workup
rows: Selective suppression test; CT/adrenal venous sampling
Plasma free or urine fractionated metanephrines

secondary-hypertension.evidence: Aldosterone screening checked 2026-10-30: [Endocrine Society 2025](https://www.endocrine.org/clinical-practice-guidelines/primary-aldosteronism-2); other causes: established teaching.

skin-cancer.name: Skin cancer
skin-cancer.scope: Actinic keratosis, squamous cell carcinoma, basal cell carcinoma, melanoma, photoprotection and sunscreen
skin-cancer.core: Changing pigmented lesions or persistent keratinizing, pearly, or ulcerated growths require examination and tissue diagnosis rather than empiric reassurance.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: UV exposure, fair skin, sunburns, tanning beds, older age; immunosuppression particularly increases SCC
Melanoma: numerous/atypical nevi, family/personal melanoma history; may arise without a preexisting nevus
Chronic wounds/scars predispose SCC; acral melanoma occurs regardless of skin pigmentation

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Melanoma: **ABCDE**—asymmetry, border irregularity, color variation, diameter, evolution; ugly-duckling lesion
Diameter >6 mm concerning, but smaller evolving lesions still require biopsy
Amelanotic melanoma may be pink; inspect soles, palms, nail beds; nail pigment extending onto fold concerning
Rapid growth, bleeding, nonhealing ulcer, fixation, neurologic symptoms, nodes → aggressive or advanced disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: UV-induced DNA damage → keratinocyte malignancy; melanocyte transformation causes melanoma
AK represents dysplastic keratinocytes with potential progression to invasive SCC

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspicious melanoma → **full-thickness excisional biopsy with narrow margins** to measure Breslow depth
Partial biopsy acceptable when complete excision impractical; avoid superficial sampling that prevents staging
Suspected keratinocyte carcinoma → deep shave or punch biopsy; <1 cm → **narrow-margin excisional biopsy**
AK persisting after topical fluorouracil → **excisional biopsy** to exclude invasive SCC
Breslow thickness/ulceration guide melanoma staging; sentinel-node discussion generally at ≥0.8 mm or ulceration

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Localized invasive cancers → **surgical excision**; high-risk/recurrent facial BCC/SCC → Mohs
Low-risk BCC → **excision with narrow margins (≤1 cm)**; no sentinel node biopsy
Positive margin on BCC/SCC → **reexcision** or Mohs, not observation
★ Melanoma → **wide local excision after diagnostic biopsy**; margins depend on depth
Advanced melanoma → specialist immunotherapy, selected BRAF-targeted drugs; avoid destructive treatment before diagnosis

rows.label: Complications
items: BCC: extensive local destruction, rare metastasis; SCC: nodal metastasis, especially high-risk sites/immunosuppression
Melanoma: distant metastases, including brain; immunotherapy → colitis, endocrinopathies, pneumonitis

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Broad-spectrum SPF ≥30**, reapply every 2 hours/outdoors after swimming; shade, protective clothing, no tanning
Infants <6 months → **shade, protective clothing**; avoid sunscreen
Self-examination, postcancer follow-up; suspicious lesions require evaluation despite uncertain population-screening benefit

rows.label: Mimics
items: Seborrheic keratosis: waxy stuck-on plaque; atypical lesions still biopsy
Dermatofibroma: firm papule with dimple sign
Benign nevus: stable symmetric uniform, <6 mm → **observation**, even with melanoma family history
Congenital melanocytic nevus: brown lesion from birth, may darken or grow coarse hair

table.title: Nonmelanoma patterns
rows: Nonhealing scaly indurated plaque/ulcer/nodule; lip/ear common
Assess high-risk features and regional nodes
Pearly rolled edge, telangiectasia, central ulcer
Treat despite slow growth; local invasion

skin-cancer.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [AAD melanoma guidance](https://www.aad.org/member/clinical-quality/guidelines/melanoma); established keratinocyte-cancer and photoprotection teaching.

supraventricular-tachycardia.name: Supraventricular tachycardia
supraventricular-tachycardia.scope: AVNRT, AVRT, focal atrial tachycardia, vagal maneuvers, adenosine, synchronized cardioversion, catheter ablation
supraventricular-tachycardia.core: Abrupt rapid regular palpitations with a usually narrow QRS often represent AV-node-dependent reentry; stability determines immediate electrical versus pharmacologic treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Accessory pathway, prior episodes, adrenergic triggers, caffeine/stimulants
Focal atrial tachycardia may accompany structural disease; incessant forms can cause cardiomyopathy

rows.label: Clues
items: Regular rate often 150–250/min; palpitations, lightheadedness, dyspnea, neck pounding
★ **Hypotension, shock, ischemic chest pain, altered mentation**, or acute HF → unstable tachycardia
WPW between episodes: short PR, delta wave, widened QRS; may be absent with concealed pathway

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Reentry requires distinct conduction/refractory properties; AV node participates in AVNRT and orthodromic AVRT
Adenosine transiently blocks AV conduction; automatic atrial rhythms may continue despite transient ventricular slowing

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **12-lead ECG during episode**, continuous rhythm monitoring; check electrolytes, medication/exposure triggers
Wide-complex rhythm uncertain → presume VT rather than casually applying narrow-complex algorithm
Structural concern → echocardiography; recurrent undocumented events → ambulatory monitoring/electrophysiology evaluation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Unstable with pulse → **synchronized cardioversion**; sedation if feasible without delaying rescue
★ Stable regular narrow rhythm → **modified Valsalva → rapid IV adenosine**
Persistent stable SVT → IV diltiazem/verapamil or beta blocker if no contraindication; cardioversion if unsuccessful
★ Irregular wide preexcited AF → **procainamide or cardioversion**; avoid AV-nodal blockers, including adenosine
Recurrent symptomatic AVNRT/AVRT or focal tachycardia → catheter ablation; selected patients use oral nodal blockers

rows.label: Complications
items: Syncope, demand ischemia, tachycardia-mediated cardiomyopathy; preexcited AF can degenerate to VF
Adenosine: brief flushing/chest pressure, bronchospasm; avoid in active severe bronchospasm

rows.label: Prevention
items: Teach vagal maneuver, limit personal triggers; discuss definitive ablation for recurrence
Ablation near AV node carries small heart-block risk; shared procedural decision

rows.label: Mimics
items: Sinus tachycardia: gradual rate changes, beat-to-beat variability, physiologic driver; infants rarely >220/min
Atrial flutter: atrial sawtooth waves, often ventricular rate near 150

supraventricular-tachycardia.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [AHA adult advanced life support](https://cpr.heart.org/en/resuscitation-science/cpr-and-ecc-guidelines/adult-advanced-life-support), [ACC/AHA AF guideline (2023)](https://www.jacc.org/doi/10.1016/j.jacc.2023.08.017).

sympathomimetic-toxicity.name: Sympathomimetic toxicity
sympathomimetic-toxicity.scope: Cocaine, amphetamines, methamphetamine, sympathomimetic toxidrome, benzodiazepines, cooling, avoidance of pure beta-blockers
sympathomimetic-toxicity.core: Stimulant exposure produces agitation, diaphoresis, mydriasis, hypertension, tachycardia, and hyperthermia; sedation limits dangerous catecholamine excess.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Cocaine, amphetamines, methamphetamine, synthetic cathinones; prescription stimulant misuse
Coingested alcohol forms cocaethylene with cocaine, increasing cardiotoxicity; exertion/heat worsens injury

rows.label: Clues
items: Paranoia, psychosis, seizures, chest pain; bowel sounds usually active
★ **Severe hyperthermia, acidosis, rigidity/agitation, arrhythmia** → life-threatening poisoning
Cocaine additionally blocks sodium channels, producing QRS widening
MDMA: bruxism, diaphoresis, hyperthermia, severe **hyponatremia** from water intake and SIADH

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Cocaine inhibits monoamine reuptake; amphetamines increase release → adrenergic/dopaminergic overstimulation
Vasoconstriction, increased oxygen demand, platelet activation → myocardial/cerebral ischemia

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical toxidrome**; temperature, glucose, ECG, electrolytes, creatinine, CK, urinalysis
Chest pain → serial ECG/troponin; neurologic deficit/severe headache → head CT for hemorrhage/stroke
Urine immunoassay supports exposure but false positives/negatives occur; never delay stabilization for results

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Benzodiazepines first** for agitation, seizures, tachycardia, hypertension; airway support when necessary
★ **Rapid external cooling + IV crystalloids** for hyperthermia/rhabdomyolysis; antipyretics ineffective
Persistent severe hypertension/vasospasm → nitroglycerin, nicardipine, or phentolamine after sedation
★ Acute cocaine toxicity: **avoid pure beta-blocker monotherapy**; unopposed alpha vasoconstriction concern
Wide QRS ventricular toxicity → sodium bicarbonate; ACS evaluation and aspirin when bleeding contraindications absent

rows.label: Complications
items: MI, aortic dissection, ischemic/hemorrhagic stroke, seizures, rhabdomyolysis, AKI, DIC
Methamphetamine: formication, dental decay, psychosis, cardiomyopathy; cocaine snorting: rhinitis, septal perforation; pregnancy: abruption

rows.label: Prevention
items: Offer addiction treatment and contingency management; assess depression and suicidality after stimulant crash
Harm-reduction counseling, avoid mixing substances; naloxone access for possible opioid contamination

rows.label: Mimics
items: Anticholinergic toxicity: dry skin, urinary retention, reduced bowel sounds
Serotonin syndrome: inducible/spontaneous clonus, hyperreflexia; NMS: dopamine blockade, lead-pipe rigidity
Thyroid storm: thyroid disease with sustained systemic hypermetabolism
PCP: rotatory/vertical nystagmus, violent agitation; also sedate with benzodiazepines

testicular-torsion.name: Testicular torsion
testicular-torsion.scope: Testicular torsion, absent cremasteric reflex, bell-clapper deformity, Doppler ultrasound, surgical detorsion and bilateral orchiopexy
testicular-torsion.core: Sudden unilateral scrotal pain with vomiting in an adolescent is spermatic cord torsion until excluded; salvage depends on immediate action.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Bell-clapper deformity permits excessive intravaginal rotation; often bilateral anatomic predisposition
Pubertal peak; may follow sleep, activity, or minor trauma; neonates can have extravaginal torsion

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **High-riding horizontal testis, absent cremasteric reflex**, diffuse tenderness and swelling
Pain may present as lower abdominal discomfort without volunteered scrotal symptoms
Prior self-resolving attacks suggest intermittent torsion; symptom resolution does not eliminate recurrence risk
Delayed fever/erythema can occur; no single examination finding reliably excludes torsion

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Cord rotation obstructs venous drainage then arterial inflow → progressive ischemia
Viability falls rapidly with delay; greatest salvage when detorsion occurs within about 6 hours

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ High clinical suspicion → **immediate urologic exploration**, no imaging delay
Equivocal presentation → **color Doppler ultrasound**, comparing perfusion with opposite testis
Reduced/absent flow or twisted cord supports diagnosis; preserved flow possible in partial/intermittent torsion
Urinalysis for infection if uncertain; pyuria does not automatically exclude simultaneous torsion
Examine both testes in boys with unexplained acute abdominal pain; ultrasound cannot overrule compelling clinical findings

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Urgent surgical detorsion + bilateral orchiopexy**; orchiectomy only if nonviable
NPO, IV analgesia, fluids as needed; call urology while preparing operation
★ If surgical delay unavoidable → **manual outward detorsion** as bridge; direction sometimes reversed
Pain relief after manual detorsion still requires operative confirmation and fixation; residual twisting possible

rows.label: Complications
items: Infarction, testicular loss, later atrophy, reduced fertility; endocrine function often maintained by opposite testis
Reperfusion does not guarantee long-term viability; follow-up for atrophy

rows.label: Prevention
items: Contralateral fixation addresses shared anatomy; evaluate recurrent episodic scrotal pain promptly
Teach adolescents to report sudden pain immediately despite embarrassment

rows.label: Mimics
items: Epididymitis: gradual pain, urinary/STI symptoms, increased epididymal Doppler flow
Appendix testis torsion: focal superior-pole tenderness, blue-dot sign, preserved testicular flow
Incarcerated hernia: irreducible inguinoscrotal mass, possible bowel obstruction

testicular-torsion.evidence: Not checked online; established urologic emergency assessment and salvage principles.

traumatic-brain-injury.name: Traumatic brain injury
traumatic-brain-injury.scope: Epidural hematoma, subdural hematoma, cerebral contusion, diffuse axonal injury, concussion, elevated ICP
traumatic-brain-injury.core: Head trauma ranges from transient functional disturbance to expanding hemorrhage; serial neurologic deterioration requires urgent imaging and neurosurgical assessment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Falls, crashes, assault, sports; anticoagulants, antiplatelets, bleeding disorders
Older age, alcohol use and cerebral atrophy predispose to bridging-vein injury

rows.label: Clues
items: Headache, vomiting, amnesia; focal deficit or progressive somnolence suggests structural injury; hemiparesis → contralateral supratentorial mass
★ **Unilateral fixed dilated pupil + declining consciousness** → uncal herniation
Cushing response: hypertension, bradycardia, irregular breathing; late sign of ↑ICP

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Impact/shear → ischemia, excitotoxicity; **cerebral edema** → deterioration over 1–3 days, brainstem reflex loss
Rising intracranial volume → ↓cerebral perfusion; hypotension/hypoxia worsen secondary injury

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ ABCs/cervical protection → **GCS, pupils, focal examination**, repeated serially
**Noncontrast head CT** for moderate/severe injury or mild injury with high-risk features
High-risk features: anticoagulation, skull-fracture signs, focal deficit, repeated vomiting, worsening symptoms
GCS 13–15 mild, 9–12 moderate, ≤8 severe

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **GCS ≤8 or hypoventilation → intubate before imaging/surgery**; avoid hypoxemia/hypotension; reverse anticoagulants
Expanding hematoma, mass effect or deterioration → urgent neurosurgical evacuation
★ Elevated ICP → head elevation, analgesia/sedation, **hypertonic saline or mannitol**; treat sustained ICP >22 mm Hg
Herniation → brief hyperventilation as bridge; no prophylactic hyperventilation or corticosteroids
Severe/high-risk TBI → levetiracetam for 7 days; refractory ICP → neurosurgical decompression

rows.label: Complications
items: Posttraumatic seizures, chronic cognitive/behavioral impairment, postconcussion syndrome, hydrocephalus
Skull-base fracture → CSF leak/meningitis; no nasal instrumentation
Frontal contusion → **executive dysfunction**: impaired conceptual planning, judgment, motivation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Seatbelts, helmets, fall prevention
Concussion: no same-day sports; relative rest 24–48 hours → graded recovery
Persistent symptoms, even normal CT → **no contact sports** until reassessed; second-impact risk

rows.label: Mimics
items: Intoxication: may coexist; exclude intracranial injury first
Hypoglycemia: check glucose in any altered mental status

table.title: Injury patterns
rows: Temporal impact; middle meningeal artery; lucid interval
Bridging-vein rupture; acute or weeks-later fluctuating decline
Crescent; crosses sutures, limited by dural reflections
Immediate prolonged coma after rotational acceleration
Transient LOC, amnesia, headache, vomiting; normal neurologic exam

traumatic-brain-injury.evidence: Acute management checked 2026-10-30: [ACS TBI best practices, 2024](https://www.facs.org/media/vgfgjpfk/best-practices-guidelines-traumatic-brain-injury.pdf).

vaginitis.name: Vaginitis
vaginitis.scope: Bacterial vaginosis, Trichomoniasis, Vulvovaginal candidiasis, atrophic vaginitis, genitourinary syndrome of menopause
vaginitis.core: Vaginal discharge or irritation requires distinction among dysbiosis, sexually transmitted protozoal infection, yeast overgrowth, and hypoestrogenic mucosal change.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: BV: new partners, douching; trichomoniasis: sexual exposure
Candida: antibiotics, pregnancy, diabetes, immunosuppression; atrophy: menopause or other hypoestrogenic states
Prepubertal: hand inoculation of respiratory pathogens during URI

rows.label: Clues
items: Pruritus, dysuria, dyspareunia; discharge appearance overlaps, so symptoms alone insufficient
★ **Fever, lower abdominal pain, cervical motion tenderness** → evaluate PID rather than isolated vaginitis
Postmenopausal bleeding needs assessment beyond assuming atrophy
★ Prepubertal **foul purulent/bloody discharge** → retained vaginal **foreign body**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: BV: lactobacilli depleted, anaerobes expand; Candida causes inflammatory overgrowth
Low estrogen thins epithelium and reduces lactobacilli → mucosal fragility and elevated vaginal pH

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Vaginal pH, saline/KOH microscopy**, history and examination; NAAT improves infectious diagnosis
BV: ≥3 Amsel—discharge, ↑pH, clue cells, amine odor; Gardnerella culture unhelpful (normal flora)
★ Suspected trichomoniasis + negative wet mount → **NAAT**, not reassurance
Recurrent/complicated Candida → culture or PCR for species; asymptomatic colonization alone needs no treatment

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Trichomoniasis → **oral metronidazole 7 days in women**; treat partners, abstain until completed/resolved
BV → oral metronidazole 7 days or vaginal metronidazole/clindamycin, **no routine partner treatment**, ACOG: treat if recurrent; treat symptomatic pregnancy
Candida → topical azole/nystatin or oral fluconazole; **pregnancy: topical azole 7 days**, avoid oral fluconazole
GSM → moisturizers/lubricants, then low-dose vaginal estrogen for persistent symptoms
Recurrent BV: ACOG 2025 considers male-partner metronidazole + topical clindamycin; older boards omit

rows.label: Complications
items: BV/trichomoniasis associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes and increased STI acquisition
Recurrent symptoms → reassess diagnosis, adherence, reinfection, diabetes or resistant/non-albicans yeast

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Trichomoniasis → **retest women at about 3 months**; condoms
Avoid douching/irritants; no routine partner treatment for uncomplicated Candida

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cervicitis: endocervical mucopus, friability, positive GC/CT NAAT
Contact dermatitis: external irritation after product exposure
Sarcoma botryoides: girl with bleeding, grape-like polypoid vaginal mass
